findings.claim: The module already has a validator meant to require the action UUID, but it never runs because it is registered for the wrong class. This PR adds a second, working UUID rule in the resource and leaves the dead validator as a misleading duplicate.
findings.evidence: api/src/main/java/org/openmrs/module/stockmanagement/api/validator/StockOperationActionValidator.java:12 declares @Handler(supports = { StockOperationDTO.class }) while supports() and validate() target StockOperationAction. The validator checks `getUuid() == null` (not blank) and uses the 'namerequired' message key for uuid. It has been like this since 94c3a9a (2023-01-29). DelegatingCrudResource.create (webservices.rest 3.0.0) calls ValidateUtil.validate(delegate) before save(). I ran a throwaway BaseModuleContextSensitiveTest on core 2.8.0. HandlerUtil.getHandlersForType(Validator.class, StockOperationAction.class) returned [], and ValidateUtil.validate on a SUBMIT action with a null UUID passed. Control: after retargeting @Handler to StockOperationAction.class, the same probe threw ValidationException 'uuid: Name is required'. It also threw 'reason: Please provide a reason' for a REJECT with no reason. Retargeting therefore also enables reason rules that nothing enforces today: the modal (esm stock-operations.modal.tsx handleClick) does not block an empty reason, and StockManagementServiceImpl.processStockOperationAction:1835 has no reason check. The PR's resource guard is a reasonable fix in scope. The ask is to record or remove the dead validator rule (or fix its registration as a follow-up), so the UUID rule doesn't live in two places that disagree (== null vs isBlank).

verdict: Ready to merge: the guard closes the ticket's backend half for null, empty and whitespace UUIDs on every action, and its tests go red when it is removed or weakened. The only finding is non-blocking: a mis-registered, dead StockOperationActionValidator that already claims to enforce the same rule.
what_i_swept: Step 1: PR body, O3-6201 snapshot, diff stat (3 files, +131/-1; three-dot and two-dot diffs match, so the branch is not behind master). Step 2: confirmed the ticket's cause at StockManagementDao.java:719 (filter skipped when the UUID is blank), so the resource guard on the only caller that acts on the result fixes the cause. Compared against siblings: saveStockOperationBatchNumbers already guards blank UUIDs in the service (StockManagementServiceImpl ~3320), and StockOperationActionValidator is the unused intended guard (F1). Accounted for each hunk: the guard (required), ObjectNotFoundException for unknown UUIDs (described in the PR; previously RestClientException), and omod/pom.xml openmrs-test (required because omod had no tests on master; mirrors api/pom.xml). Step 3: ran StockOperationActionResourceTest at head (4 pass), then three mutations: guard removed (1 failure + 1 error), isBlank->isEmpty (1 failure), ObjectNotFoundException->RestClientException (1 error). Read the REST 3.0.0 BaseRestController.handleException and the @ResponseStatus on IllegalRequestException (400) and ObjectNotFoundException (404), and DelegatingCrudResource.create. Outward trace: the frontend caller (stock-operations.modal.tsx) and extractErrorMessagesFromResponse read responseBody.error.message, which works with the 400 body. git grep for other setStockOperationUuid/get(0) callers: sendStockOperationNotification takes an internal UUID; StockOperationResource.getByUniqueId and StockOperationBatchNumbersResource.getByUniqueId pass the URL id through, but they are read-only. Build config: diffed the omod dependency:tree for master vs head (adds the test-scope openmrs-test tree; provided-scope byte-buddy 1.12.18->1.14.8 and snakeyaml 2.4->2.2) and packaged both, and the .omod entry lists are identical (3 lib/ entries). Validator registration was driven with a real context-sensitive probe plus a control.
could_not_verify: The end-to-end HTTP status through a running REST 3.0 dispatcher servlet needs access I don't have: no OpenMRS server is available. Instead I checked handleException directly, as the PR's own test does, and read the @ResponseStatus annotations.

Whether GET /stockoperation/%20 actually reaches getByUniqueId(" ") and returns the newest visible operation needs access I don't have (a running server and Spring path decoding). It is read-only and outside the ticket, so I did not raise it as a finding.
notes: Pass 1 found F1. Pass 2 established F1's cost (re-enabling the reason rules) and checked the build/pom hunk. Pass 3 found nothing new.
